content.text:
The drawing shows an oxindole core: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered lactam. The ring carbon at position 3 carries an OH, the carbon at position 2 is a C=O, and the nitrogen carries a benzyl group (Bn). This is 1-benzyl-3-hydroxyindolin-2-one.

C3 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I include no stereochemistry.

Writing the SMILES: O=C1N(Cc2ccccc2)c2ccccc2C1O

Atom check:
- C1 is the carbonyl carbon, written `O=C1`.
- N is bonded to the benzyl CH2 and the phenyl group, written `N(Cc2ccccc2)`.
- The fused benzene is `c2ccccc2`, closing back onto the aromatic carbon that bears C3.
- `C1O` is C3 with its OH, which closes the five-membered ring to the carbonyl carbon.

SMILES: O=C1N(Cc2ccccc2)c2ccccc2C1O
